title: Supervising Crypto-Asset Service Providers under MiCA (EU Edition)
summary: An advanced fifteen-module programme equipping EU national competent authorities to authorise and supervise crypto-asset service providers and token issuers under MiCA.
intro: This training programme equips national competent authority staff to authorise and supervise crypto-asset service providers and token issuers under MiCA: assessing business models, governance, prudential resources, custody and resilience, and acting on market abuse, financial crime and cross-border risks.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors a rigorous, practical command of MiCA and the wider EU rulebook that surrounds it, from the technology and business models through to authorisation, ongoing supervision, enforcement and crisis management. Participants leave able to look beyond a firm's documentation, identify red flags early and apply MiCA's supervisory powers proportionately, working with ESMA, the EBA and other national competent authorities.
sections.What It Covers: Distributed ledger technology and the crypto ecosystem, MiCA's scope, taxonomy and rulebook, CASP business models, governance and prudential requirements, authorisation and risk-based supervision, ICT risk under DORA, custody and safeguarding, market abuse, AML/CFT and the Travel Rule, asset-referenced and e-money tokens, passporting and cooperation, and enforcement, crisis management and emerging risks.
Intended Audience: Authorisation, supervision and inspection staff responsible for crypto-asset service providers and token issuers
AML/CFT, market integrity, ICT risk and enforcement specialists covering digital finance
Heads of department and senior managers setting the authority's crypto-asset supervisory strategy
Learning Objectives: Explain how distributed ledgers, crypto-assets and CASP business models work and where risk sits
Apply MiCA's scope, taxonomy and Level 1 to Level 3 rulebook to authorisation and ongoing supervision
Assess CASP governance, prudential resources, custody and operational resilience, including under DORA
Evaluate market abuse, AML/CFT, Travel Rule and sanctions risks and the controls that address them
Operate passporting, information exchange and colleges with other authorities, ESMA and the EBA
Apply graduated enforcement and crisis tools, and anticipate emerging risks in digital finance
sections.Structure and Format: Fifteen modules of about five hours each, organised in five pathways and delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a full programme over several weeks or pathway by pathway. Each module combines pre-reading and a technical briefing with case studies, red-flag exercises and supervisory question sets, and pathways or modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's needs.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of authorising or supervising financial firms is helpful. No technical background in blockchain is required, as the first pathway builds the foundations.
Core Reading: Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 on information accompanying transfers of funds and certain crypto-assets (Transfer of Funds Regulation)
Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)
FSB, High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Crypto-Asset Activities and Markets (2023)

modules.title: Blockchain and Distributed Ledgers for Supervisors
modules.summary: How blockchain and distributed ledgers work in digital finance, where control really sits, and the technological failure modes that drive consumer harm, prudential loss and operational incidents at CASPs.
objectives: Explain how distributed ledgers validate, record and execute transactions
Distinguish public, permissioned and hybrid ledgers and the supervisory leverage each allows
Identify the true control points and failure modes behind crypto incidents
syllabus: Digital money versus electronic money: who owes what to whom
Validation, cryptography, tamper-evident records and smart contracts
Control points: upgrades, pause functions, administrator keys, forks and listings
Failure modes: code flaws, oracle manipulation, bridges and off-chain dependencies

modules.title: The Crypto Ecosystem: Assets, Tokenisation and Market Structure
modules.summary: Maps the participants in crypto markets, from protocol developers and token issuers to trading venues, custodians and end users, and how value, risk and accountability flow between them.
objectives: Map ecosystem participants to accountability and control points
Analyse the economic incentives that create concentration and integrity risk
Recognise red flags in tokenisation and market infrastructure providers
syllabus: Networks, issuers, validators, wallets, venues, brokers and market makers
Tokenisation: tokenised assets, utility tokens and stablecoins
Incentives, concentration and conflicts in crypto market structure
Resilience of networks, bridges, oracles and infrastructure providers

modules.title: MiCA Fundamentals: Objectives, Scope and Architecture
modules.summary: MiCA's objectives, perimeter and taxonomy, how Level 1 is built out through ESMA and EBA technical standards and guidelines, and where gaps and ambiguity create supervisory risk.
objectives: Explain MiCA's objectives and its place within the wider EU financial services rulebook
Apply MiCA's taxonomy and perimeter, including the boundary with financial instruments
Use the full Level 1, 2 and 3 rulebook in authorisation and thematic work
syllabus: Consumer protection, market integrity and financial stability objectives
ARTs, EMTs and other crypto-assets; the boundary with MiFID financial instruments
Perimeter questions: NFTs issued in series, fractionalisation and DeFi
Roles of the Commission, ESMA, the EBA and national competent authorities

modules.title: CASP Business Models and the CeFi–DeFi Spectrum
modules.summary: The business models of trading platforms, brokers, custodians, issuers and other providers, where MiCA obligations attach to each, and how supervisors use business model analysis to test viability and conflicts.
objectives: Map crypto business models to MiCA's crypto-asset services
Identify the prudential and conduct risks of each model
Use business model analysis to stress-test viability and conflicts of interest
syllabus: The CeFi–DeFi spectrum and where MiCA obligations attach in practice
Trading platforms, exchange, execution, custody, advice and portfolio management services
Red flags: venues acting as market maker, opaque fees, own-token reserves
Group structures designed to fragment regulatory obligations

modules.title: Governance, Risk Management and Internal Controls in CASPs
modules.summary: How to look beneath governance documentation to judge whether a CASP's management body, control functions and internal controls work in practice, and how to respond when they do not.
objectives: Assess the management body, suitability and conflicts of interest controls against MiCA
Evaluate the independence, resources and influence of risk, compliance and internal audit
Apply proportionate intervention to governance and control weaknesses
syllabus: MiCA governance requirements: management body, shareholders, conflicts and complaints
Three lines of defence and risk appetite in a crypto-asset business
Red flags: founder dominance, nominal independence, marginalised control functions
Governance of CASPs within wider groups, including non-EU parents

modules.title: Prudential Risk, Financial Resources and Sustainability
modules.summary: MiCA's prudential requirements for CASPs and token issuers, how capital and liquidity behave across the crypto market cycle, and how supervisors identify financially fragile firms before they fail.
objectives: Apply MiCA's own funds requirements to different CASP classes and issuer types
Assess liquidity, revenue volatility and reliance on affiliate funding
Select supervisory tools from enhanced monitoring to recovery plan requirements
syllabus: Permanent minimum capital and fixed overhead requirements for CASPs
Own funds, reserve and liquidity requirements for ART and EMT issuers
Prudential red flags: thin capital, untested projections, affiliate exposures
Financial analysis, stress testing, peer benchmarking and early warning indicators

modules.title: Authorising Crypto-Asset Service Providers
modules.summary: Running a consistent, proportionate MiCA authorisation gateway: assessing the application dossier, substance and group dependencies, and resolving material issues before authorisation rather than deferring them to supervision.
objectives: Assess the programme of operations, governance, prudential safeguards and ICT arrangements
Test substance, group dependencies and outsourcing to prevent letter-box entities
Apply service-specific focus to trading platforms, brokers and custodians
syllabus: Gateway design: completeness thresholds, risk-based prioritisation and early challenge
Forward-looking review of business plans, growth assumptions and scalability
Transitional regime, notification route for licensed firms and prior regulatory history
Authorising a cross-border hub: passporting implications from day one

modules.title: Risk-Based Supervision of CASPs in Practice
modules.summary: Designing and operating a risk-based supervisory model for CASPs: prioritising resources, monitoring between engagements, running inspections and using MiCA's supervisory powers to drive and verify remediation.
objectives: Design a risk framework that prioritises CASPs by impact and probability of harm
Use regulatory data and market intelligence to set escalation triggers
Plan, conduct and follow up on-site inspections of CASPs
syllabus: Firm risk assessment, supervisory planning and resource allocation
Early warning signals: rapid growth, control function turnover, incidents
Inspection methodology: document requests, interviews, walkthroughs and customer journeys
Using MiCA's supervisory powers and keeping a defensible decision trail

modules.title: Operational Resilience: ICT Risk and DORA
modules.summary: How DORA applies to CASPs alongside MiCA's organisational requirements, the ICT risks specific to crypto operations, and how supervisors assess resilience and use incident reports as early warning.
objectives: Explain DORA's ICT risk, incident reporting, testing and third-party requirements for CASPs
Identify crypto-specific ICT risks in key management, cloud and on-chain/off-chain links
Assess resilience arrangements and respond when standards are not met
syllabus: DORA applied to CASPs and its interaction with MiCA
Key management, hot and cold wallet segregation and cloud concentration
Incident classification and reporting as a supervisory early warning tool
Resilience testing, register of information and third-party exit provisions

modules.title: Wallets, Custody and Safeguarding of Crypto-Assets
modules.summary: How crypto-asset custody works in practice, from hot and cold storage to multi-party computation and sub-custody chains, and how supervisors verify that client assets are safeguarded and segregated.
objectives: Explain custody architectures and how each affects the risk to client assets
Identify key management, reconciliation, sub-custody and asset misuse risks
Verify custody arrangements against MiCA safeguarding and liability requirements
syllabus: Keys, wallets, hardware security modules, multi-signature and MPC
Custody policies, client agreements, segregation and return of assets
Red flags: weak reconciliation, single-person key access, affiliated sub-custody
Custodian liability for loss and client assets on insolvency

modules.title: Market Integrity: Preventing Crypto Market Abuse
modules.summary: MiCA's market abuse regime and how it adapts established market abuse concepts to crypto, the manipulation schemes specific to crypto markets, and how supervisors assess surveillance and use order reports as intelligence.
objectives: Explain MiCA's prohibitions on insider dealing, unlawful disclosure and manipulation
Detect crypto-native manipulation, including wash trading, spoofing and MEV extraction
Assess CASP surveillance systems and suspicious transaction and order reporting
syllabus: Inside information in token issuance, listings and CASP operations
Wash trading, pump-and-dump schemes, spoofing and MEV
Surveillance calibration, investigation workflows and STORs as intelligence
Cross-venue analysis, enforcement referral and cross-border cooperation

modules.title: Financial Crime: AML/CFT and the Travel Rule
modules.summary: Illicit finance typologies in crypto markets, the EU AML framework and Transfer of Funds Regulation as they apply to CASPs, and how supervisors test controls and coordinate with the national FIU.
objectives: Identify money laundering and terrorist financing typologies in crypto markets
Evaluate due diligence, transaction monitoring, Travel Rule compliance and the MLRO function
Coordinate AML/CFT findings with the AML supervisor and the national FIU
syllabus: Typologies: mixers, high-risk jurisdictions, money mules and rapid layering
Blockchain analytics: capabilities, limits and use as a supervisory check
The Travel Rule under the Transfer of Funds Regulation, including self-hosted wallets
The EU AML package and the interaction between MiCA and AMLR

modules.title: Stablecoins: Asset-Referenced and E-Money Tokens
modules.summary: How ARTs and EMTs are structured and regulated under MiCA Titles III and IV, the reserve and redemption mechanics that determine stability, and the EBA's role for significant tokens.
objectives: Distinguish fiat-backed, collateralised and algorithmic designs and their risk profiles
Evaluate reserve quality, liquidity and redemption resilience under stress
Explain significance classification and the supervisory handover to the EBA
syllabus: Stablecoin models and lessons from algorithmic stablecoin collapses
Reserve composition, custody, audit and redemption at par on demand
EMTs and electronic money: interplay with PSD2 and the payments framework
Significant tokens: EBA supervision, colleges and recovery and redemption plans

modules.title: Passporting, Sanctions and Supervisory Cooperation
modules.summary: How MiCA passporting works for home and host authorities, the sanctions obligations that apply to crypto operations, and the cooperation mechanisms linking national competent authorities, ESMA and the EBA.
objectives: Manage home and host responsibilities for passporting CASPs
Assess sanctions screening, including wallet screening and self-hosted wallet controls
Operate information exchange and coordinated responses to cross-border concerns
syllabus: Passport notifications, reverse solicitation limits and host authority powers
Letter-box risk, substance and home–host information gaps
Significant CASPs, ESMA convergence tools and peer reviews
Sanctions evasion typologies and EU restrictive measures in crypto markets

modules.title: Enforcement, Crisis Management and Emerging Risks
modules.summary: Using MiCA's graduated enforcement toolkit, managing a CASP in distress through to orderly wind-down, and anticipating emerging risks in digital finance, ending with a capstone crisis simulation.
objectives: Apply MiCA's supervisory measures and penalties proportionately and with sound process
Manage a CASP crisis from early distress to orderly wind-down and cross-border coordination
Assess emerging risks and their implications for supervisory strategy and capability
syllabus: From supervisory measures to fines, public warnings and withdrawal of authorisation
Lessons from major crypto exchange and crypto lender failures
Emerging risks: DeFi, tokenised infrastructure, AI-driven trading and the digital euro
Workshop: CASP failure crisis simulation

related.title: MiCA Essentials for Supervisors (EU Edition)
related.summary: A six-module essentials programme giving EU national competent authority staff a practical command of MiCA, from token regimes and CASP authorisation to supervision and enforcement.

related.title: Crypto and Blockchain Fundamentals
related.summary: A ten-module foundation programme giving supervisors a practical understanding of blockchain, crypto-asset markets and service providers, and the risks they must supervise.

related.title: Crypto-Asset Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An advanced twelve-module programme equipping supervisors to authorise, supervise and take action against crypto-asset firms under comprehensive regimes and international standards.

related.title: Digital Money: Stablecoins, Tokenised Deposits and CBDCs
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and central bankers to assess stablecoins, tokenised deposits and CBDCs, and their risks to payments and financial stability.

related.title: Tokenisation of Financial Markets
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to assess tokenised securities, funds and collateral, DLT market infrastructure, settlement finality, custody and smart contract risk.

related.title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.
